179611.overview:
Billy the Kid is set in the Wild West and features William H. Bonney, the famous outlaw also known as Billy the Kid, and his adversary Sheriff Pat Garrett. Both are hired by the rancher John Tunstall to protect Lincoln County from outlaws. Unfortunately Tunstall is murdered and the two disagree how to proceed: while Garrett wants to strengthen law and order, Billy the Kid sets out to avenge Tunstall the hard way.

The player chooses between the role of Billy the Kid or Garrett which changes their goals, e.g. as Billy the Kid the player needs to build up an outlaw army. During the game, the next destination is chosen through an overhead map, e.g. the city of Santa Fe or a camp of Native Americans. In cities, the player can move, enter different buildings and talk to people in order to receive hints what to do next (sometimes hints are also received when entering one of the other locations on the map). Some people need to be bribed with money which can be earned with certain actions like robbing a bank. Often the character has to engage in action sequences, e.g. a shootout in which crosshairs are moved over the screen to shoot enemies as soon as they leave their cover. When the basic goal is reached, the game culminates in a shootout between Billy the Kid and Garrett.

180356.overview: The world is dominated by five demons, the ancient ones. Many people belong to one of the cults that worship the ancient ones. From the shadows emerges a mage that will give the sword to the only one who can defeat the evil ones and their king Morkoth -- the Lord of Destruction.

181758.overview:
La Colmena is inspired by an erotic table game (The Pyramid of Love), the purpose of which is to join together several adult people. During the course of the game, the participants will have to surpass certain tests and challenges. In the later portions of game, the tests will be more and more stimulating, and the participants will be taking off their clothes.

The game has many different sub-games, like roulette, blackjack, and poker, and during the game many general thematic questions need to be answered. It also features humorous scenes and conversations.

181760.overview:
The Smurfs: The Teletransportsmurf is a 2D platform game based on the comic by Belgian cartoonist Pierre Culliford (Peyo).

The game features two game modes. The first is a typical side-scrolling platform game in which you control a Smurf and have to save Smurfette from the evil clutches of Gargamel. Papa Smurf has found a spell for teleportation, but requires the smurf to find all the required magic ingredients that are scattered across the Smurfen lands. During the player's quest for the ingredients he can expect help from Papa Smurf.

The second game mode has mini-games for up to four players. The first player to win 10 games wins. Each game requires action and reflexes to win.

The game features multiple difficulty levels.

189988.overview: Unreleased game, partially based on Activision's earlier "Little Computer People".

205022.overview:
The Legend of Heroes is old-school JRPG with new-school sensibilities and graphics. The old-school elements of the game are its turn-based combat, linearity, long dialogue scenes, a digital pet system and lots of similar things that seem to date from the 1995-ish RPG era. There are no random fighting encounters however. In this game you control Avin in his search for his younger sister Eimelle. They were separated when their cathedral was raided by religious zealots.  
 
The word Gagharv (in the Japanese title of the remake) refers to the chasm that separates the continent Tirasweel, where the games takes place, from the rest of the world. Improvements Bandai made for this remake are completely re-done 3D graphics, new battle interface, and quicker load times.

205716.overview:
When this golf simulation was released in 1988 the U.S. National Video Game Team said it was "by far the best video golf simulation available".

1 to 4 players can tee it up on either an 18 hole American course or an 18 hole Japanese course. Players 1 & 3 share controller 1 and players 2 & 4 share controller 2.

Game modes are:

Stroke Play - The winner has the lowest number of strokes through 18 holes.
Nassau Game - The players compete against each other for points. Presses are allowed.
Practice - A single player can practice on their favorite hole.
Swing mechanics are: Press A to start the backswing, press A at the top of the swing, press A at impact. High and low shots can be selected by pressing up or down on the control pad. Right after contact another quick press of the A button at the same time as left or right will apply backspin to the ball. Complete club selection is available with the B button.

Terrain includes tee, green, fairway, out-of-bounds, water, sand (light and hard), and rough (super, light, heavy and deep).

There are four available characters:
Pretty Amy - Slow swing speed with fantastic ball control and accurate aiming.
Big Jumbo - Powerful stroke and a long hitter but good technique is needed to control his shots.
Super Mex - All-around player with average distance, accuracy and swing speed.
Miracle Chosuke - Less power than Super Mex but good at putting and unequalled accuracy. He can hit a "Reverse Miracle Putt."

212352.overview: Chess and destructive laser beams together at last! Laser Chess, which is a DOS version of the award winning original, for the most part plays like a regular chess game except that some pieces have been replaced by deflectors and a laser cannon. You move your pieces on the board as usual but have to place your deflectors in strategic positions all the while keeping an eye on your opponent doing the same thing during their turn. Turns are used up when you move a piece, rotate a piece or fire the laser. Once you feel a deflector is in the right place, unleash your laser and shoot the opposing players. Be careful though, because some pieces if rotated in the wrong direction will bounce the beam or split it in wrong directions and even worse can even bounce back at your laser cannon destroying it. Check mate means the game is done.

217792.overview:
If you’ve been to a gaming event in the past few years, you might have seen Line Wobbler, a game that creator Robin Baumgarten calls “a one-dimensional dungeon crawler.” Instead of using a conventional screen, Line Wobbler is played on a string of LED lights, which can be curved or shaped around wherever it’s set up. It’s a really fun experiment that’s surprisingly clever and nuanced for a literally one-dimensional game.

That’s one way to do a 1D game. The other way, as seen in the 1997 freeware game Lineality, is to make it a joke.

217937.overview:
Liquid War is an open-source multi-player action game based on particle flow mechanic. Thomas Colcombet developed the core concept and the original shortest path algorithm, the software was programmed by Christian Mauduit. Liquid War 6 is a GNU package distributed as free software and part of the GNU project. 

Gameplay takes place on a 2D battlefield, usually with some obstacles. Each player (2 to 6, computer or human) has an army of particles and a cursor. The objective of the game is to assimilate all enemy particles. The players can only move their cursors and cannot directly control the particles. Each particle follows the shortest path around the obstacles to its team's cursor. A player may have several thousands particles at a time, giving the collection of particles a look of a liquid blob. When a particle moves into a particle from a different team, it will fight and if the opponent particle fails to fight back (it is not moving in the opposite direction) it will eventually be assimilated by its attacker. As particles cannot die but only change teams, the total number of particles on the map remains constant. Since a particle can only fight in one direction at a time (towards its team's cursor), a player that surrounds its opponents will have a distinct advantage. The game ends when one player controls all of the particles or when the time runs out. When the time runs out, the player with the most particles wins.

217972.overview:
This game is based on the Spanish animation series of the same name, broadcast on Televisión Española during the late eighties, so as in the TV series, the action will take place in the System of the Double Sun, composed of seven planets (some inhabited and some not) and twelve moons; but the planet we should take care of is the third, where our friends live, ruled by King Brigal and his son, Prince Zalk.

Rahman, the all-powerful wizard of the kingdom, is in possession of the Magic Crown, a mysterious crown with far-reaching powers which keeps the balance of forces between him and the wicked witch Idun and her armies, led by the sinister Zohak, the witch's vizier. They live on the last three planets in the System, the Lost Planets, and you, throughout six arcade levels, must try to recover the crown, for it, you will have to deal with fantastic creatures, evil wizards and witches, helped by your strength and magical powers, until arriving at the final encounter with Rahman.

425356.overview: Lunar Catastrophe is a classic-themed megawad for Doom released on December 30, 2018. A joint-effort by partners Samantha McNallen (Miss Bubbles) & Derek Pierson (Count651), the four episode megawad is heavily inspired by Doom's abstract level design, taking inspiration not only from John Romero but Sandy Petersen and Tom Hall as well. It took two years to make, with both creators splitting the workload evenly. It was a runner-up in the Cacowards 2019.

425857.overview:
The Long Trek Back Home is a 32-map megawad for Doom II, released on 30 September 2021 by hervoheebo. Meant to be an immediate follow-up to the story of Doom II, it features maps that are heavily inspired by their original counterparts, but with a reversed progression. The player begins at the destroyed Icon of Sin site and retraces their steps through the Hell levels, city levels and finally the starport levels, while facing increasingly heavy demonic opposition and changed, mostly destroyed and twisted architecture heavily reminiscent of the original layouts. Additionally, nearly all maps feature edited versions of their respective original music tracks.

The Long Trek Back Home received an honorable mention at at the 2021 Cacowards.

426008.overview:
Li Xiaoyao is a young man who studies martial arts under the guidance of his aunt, an owner of an inn which is often visited by famous adventurers and heroes. Seeing those heroes, Li Xiaoyao dreams of becoming one himself. And of course, the mind of the young man is also occupied with pretty girls.

Finally his dream of becoming an adventurer comes true, but not quite in the fashion he wanted it to be. His aunt becomes gravely sick, and the only way to save her is to find a legendary medicine. During his journey to the land where he hopes to find the medicine, Li Xiaoyao meets the beautiful Zhao Ling'er, who is persecuted by ruthless enemies. The grand adventure of Li Xiaoyao's life begins.

Xianjian Qixia Zhuan is the first entry in the Chinese-made Legend of Sword and Fairy role-playing game series. The game is set in feudal China and features supernatural elements. Gameplay-wise, it is very close to Japanese RPGs. The player controls a party of heroes which he navigates through towns and maze-like dungeons, buying weapons and accessories and searching for treasure. Story progression is linear for the most part. There is no overworld in the game; however, some areas are seamlessly connected to each other and can be explored in a different order.

There are no random enemy encounters in the game: all enemies are visibly walking on the field and can sometimes be avoided. The turn-based battles are viewed from an isometric perspective. During the battles, the heroes can execute physical attacks, defend, use items, or execute special martial arts or spells unique to each character.

430495.overview: Discover this classic action-adventure game from Poland and join Leo the Lion on his adventures full of unexpected situations, challenges, and brawls. Travel the islands of Lion’s Archipelago and help him find the stolen crown. Try to survive in the jungle, pole, in the dungeons of the magic castle, inside pyramids and on the burnt deserts. Examine the wrecks of pirate ships on the bottom of the sea, and survive the eruption of the volcano. Experience crazy adventures and rack your brains to save Leo from traps and troubles.

447060.overview: Lurid Land is a puzzle platform game where players take the role of one of the two wizards Limbollo or Rupitto, who set out on a journey to defeat the evil wizard Cirilleus who has overtaken the kingdom of Agalonhia. In each of the 60 time-limited levels, the player's aim is to save all prisoners and open the doors to the next level, while avoiding enemies.

449626.overview:
In "The Last Warrior," you are the sole survivor of a scouting party from Earth, ambushed by countless alien ships. As the last line of defense, you rely on advanced force shields and lasers to fend off the aliens. 

The game involves destroying as many alien ships as possible before your energy depletes. Each destroyed ship is quickly replaced, adding to the challenge. Your performance is evaluated by points scored and ranks achieved: captain, major, colonel, general, or warrior. The highest ranks are reserved for the best players, with scoring details varying across game versions.

454345.overview: Los Templos Sagrados is a Spanish text-adventure, the sequel to La Diosa de Cozumel, and the second "book" of the "Ci-U-Than" trilogy of games. They all utilize the parser DAAD, that has capabilities similar to the Infocom Z-machine one (you can chain commands, correct misspellings, etc). This time around the player searches the ruins of the Yucatán peninsula for the lost mayan temple of Chichén Itzá.

454373.overview:
The LucasArts Archives Vol. I was a collection of previously released LucasArts video games sold together in one package in 1995. The set included a single user's guide that contained all instructions for each game. Star Wars Screen Entertainment was included, as well as a number of demos of Star Wars games. After the initial release for PC, The LucasArts Macintosh Archives Vol. I for Mac computers was released in early 1996, including a slightly different list of titles.
The collection was followed by second, third and fourth volumes.

455631.overview: Waste time at work efficiently! Larry has designed a program for everything you do at the office that has nothing to do with work. Create office pools, lotteries, read jokes, design memos, fax cover sheets and lots lots more! Outrageous clip art for memos and fax cover sheets will really impress your boss (try at own risk) and co-workers. "Anti-boss" safeguards help you keep your job by quickly changing your computer screen. With Laffer Utilities you may never want to do real work again!

457074.overview:
"Los lnhumanos" is a game in which our objective will be to rescue the girl who has been kidnapped by another enemy group called "Los Rokopiedras". Besides capturing our beloved, they have also committed an excess which is what really did upset Zufuru, the inhuman protagonist of this history: they have destroyed his dear Simca 1000, a unique car, full of memories of our friend.

And, as this history occurs in the city of the skyscrapers, the distant New York, Zufuru will have to cross the famous Central Park in order to find the resting four pieces of his little car. Only when all of them would be on his possession he will be able to accede to the Empire State, the second level of the game and where his beloved is located.

For the most curious, this game debts its name to a Spanish pop music group which had quite succes during the eighties, period in which they produced some of the most danced songs on the Spanish youthful and universitary circles, that's also why you can listen to some of their most famous songs during the game, as well as seeing their mascot on the game.

457629.overview: Another attempt by an unknown firm to cash in on the first Quake. This one offers a full-fledged campaign consisting of 21 levels. And the first stage, as in the original, is a location with no enemy in which the player will have to choose one of four paths, each of which symbolizes a certain complexity - Easy, Medium, Hard, Nightmare. A curiosity reserved for fans.

457814.overview: Eva lives in the year 3000 and is tasked by biologist Dr. Genus on his spaceship to search for the causes of epidemics throughout the ages. From this moment on, she must overcome a series of tests that will take her to Greek Thebes, plagued by leprosy; Hong Kong, ravaged by the plague; and 14th-century Barcelona, ​​where the Black Death killed thousands. She will later travel to Africa, Berkeley, and Paris, plagued by other epidemics, before finding Professor Luc Montagnier, who will explain the current state of the fight against AIDS.

457996.overview:
La Leyenda del Vikingo (1991) is a rare historical find from the Spanish shareware scene! It was programmed by Ángel García Delgado (A.G.D.) and distributed as a pack-in title inside Ediciones Manali's premiere issue of PC Juegos (Issue #1).

The Gameplay Loop: The game is a straightforward 2D side-scrolling or fixed-screen arcade action game. True to the era's simplistic platformer design, players control a muscular Viking warrior navigating basic landscape tiers (like icy fields or rocky shores) to battle small enemy sprites, leap across water or pit hazards, and find simple hidden treasure tokens.

The Technical Design: To guarantee maximum compatibility across early 90s Spanish home computer clones, it was heavily optimized to consume less than 512KB of system memory. The graphic engine displays the action exclusively in a high-contrast 4-color CGA graphics palette (typically utilising cyan, magenta, white, and black against a dark sky void).

458006.overview: Ediciones Manali was notorious in Spain during the early 1990s for distributing budget shareware, magazine cover disks (like PC Juegos), and compilation packs. They frequently created legally questionable, low-budget clones of major Hollywood films and video game franchises.The Copycat Premise: As a direct, unauthorized rip-off of The NeverEnding Story, the game’s original Spanish promotional material cheekily reads: "¡Imagínate! Un paisaje maravilloso y con tu mejor amigo sortea obstáculos..., pasa a mejor vida a los enemigos de siempre..., usa un arma mágica" ("Imagine! A wonderful landscape, and with your best friend, navigate obstacles..., send the usual enemies to the afterlife..., use a magic weapon.").The Gameplay: It is a rudimentary 2D side-scrolling action platformer. You control a young fantasy warrior boy (representing Atreyu) navigating linear obstacles while being accompanied by a poorly drawn, floating white-furred dragon creature (representing Falkor) to defeat fantasy critters using basic weapon strikes.

458325.overview: It all starts one fine day in the year 2000, when you find a small pyramid, which you think will bring you good luck... and then what happens happens... it will be the beginning of a journey whose final destination will be an extremely distant future.

458436.overview:
is a text-based conversational adventure based on the book "The Mystery of Silver Mountain," published in Spain by Anaya.
It was a peculiar gamebook, as at the end of its pages were lists in Basic for different platforms. The program was played alongside the book, which was required for this.

In this version, FJAP combined the two sources into a single program, allowing it to be played without the need for the original book.

The game's plot takes us to the slopes of Silver Mountain, where the Sylvans live as slaves to the bloodthirsty Grarg. Your mission is to find a series of objects that, together, have more power than the Stone of Destiny, the one that caused the situation in which the peaceful village finds itself.

An entertaining plot, many and varied descriptions, and an atmosphere that will captivate adventurous fans of the fantasy genre.

458536.overview:
Your goal is to escape from the Valshar's lair, where they have captured you to sell you to monks. You'll begin your journey in a cell, accompanied by an Elf.

This is the author's first adventure, part of the Genhag series, which also includes Rimbledén.

Although the manual warns us that it's not very good, it will surely please fans of the fantasy genre, because although the parser isn't very good, the atmosphere and the problems are engaging, with the graphics (added late) being a plus.

It's notable for being one of the few I know of that has an English version, and is included in the same package as the original.

458611.overview:
The prophecies of old speak of a cataclysm that will bring an age of pain and destruction, the Dark One responsible.

But the prophecies also speak of a young man who can sweep all this evil from the land; that young man is you.

"The Light of the Druid" is one of two adventure games in the "Legends of Lhodrye" series. In these two games, you will have to use your mental skills to solve puzzles and your keyboard skills to navigate through the screens like a platform game.

This series was born as a result of the second Video Game Contest organized by PCActual, in which it won first prize. The first two installments were later published in the Spanish magazine Computer Gaming World, and were subsequently reworked and expanded, creating two new installments translated into German, English, and Spanish for a German distribution company.

458612.overview:
Hidden, remote, and mysterious, behind the dense, leafy forests of the Elidon Kingdom lies an ancient community that houses the wisest of all the kingdom's elders. He is known to be as old as the twisted, centuries-old trees that shelter his people.

His prophecies and wisdom have illuminated even the most powerful and distant kingdoms of the continent. But in this century, his prophetic visions are tinged with strange and dark omens. Omens that foretell an imminent catastrophe, whose face is a shadow from the past, a shadow that rises once again from the darkness to seize absolute power and bring with it an era of pain and destruction.

 Likewise, the Ancient One's visions have assured the arrival of a Hero, who, through his own means and using mortal qualities—Strength, Wisdom, and Power—will ward off the evil that stalks us from the darkness and appease the Wrath of the Gods so that they do not succumb to the arrival of this new and dark form of power. The Hero will travel to the distant lands of the Kingdom of Elidon with the sole objective of reaching the Ancient One, so that he may prophesy about his mystical quest and the Hero may find a solution to his prophecies. Only the Chosen One will have the Power to defeat the darkness, and to do so, he must listen with great attention and wisdom to the Ancient One, for he will grant him the key to his Destiny and Victory.

"May the Gods be with the Chosen One and illuminate his path to Final Victory."

 The Druid's Light and Arakhas the Dark is a saga of two video adventures set in the Kingdom of Elidon, in which the protagonist must overcome various trials until reaching the game's ultimate goal: eliminating the Dark One.

This series was born as a result of the second Video Game Contest organized by PCActual, where it won first prize. The first two installments were later published in the Spanish magazine Computer Gaming World, and were subsequently reworked and expanded, creating two new installments translated into German, English, and Spanish for a German distribution company.

458730.overview: Leeds United Champions! is a managerial soccer simulation in which the player takes control of Leeds United, the English champions of the 1991/92 season, in the fourth division; the goal being to conquer the Premier League in the long run. The game is completely menu based and the sub-menus are reached through a list of icons in the main menu. In those menus the player can set all the usual options of the genre, e.g. training, transfer market, lineup, ticket prices, youth section or stadium expansion. There is no match presentation to speak of; just a screen representing a live ticker which gives out the goals and bookings. Each athlete has 15 stats which influence his performance on the field.

459131.overview: A supercomputer in the most remote part of a distant galaxy has become crazy and threatens to destroy the planet. You have been chosen to be the central link of the support command which will try to give a solution for it. But don't worry, you have been educated and trained in the Golden Ring space station, the hardest survival school of the galactic confederation. Besides, your ship is equipped with the ultimate devices which will allow you to travel safely by the well-known universe. The Combat Mode, where you can activate a panel with a system to locate and to destroy your enemies and the Control System via Menus, both make La Aventura Espacial a new concept in the graphic-conversational adventure. First of all, your mission is to find your companions, whom are distributed by all the universe, and together with them you must arrive to the central base of the Dark Threat. There, you will have to deal one on one with the computer. It's not an easy task, but you are the last hope of the humanity. All the galaxy has its destiny in your hands.

459132.overview: A bicycling simulation where you recruit a team and then watch the results.

459771.overview: If anything characterized Dinamic, it was its commercial and marketing expertise, and I don't think the game would have sold as well if it didn't feature a well-known character. What stood out about this game was its theme, as well as the carefully crafted presentation of the box... It kept you hooked for quite some time, both for the quality of its graphics and its atmosphere. Despite the fact that the number "1" appeared on the spine of the box, as if implying that there would be more adventures based on Vázquez Montalbán's character, only this installment, the work of Fabián Escalante (also the author of another good adventure, Ke Rulen los Petas), was ultimately completed.

465764.overview: Labyrinth is an early maze game with 10 different ways to play. Points are lost by making contact with the edges of the labyrinth

465766.overview: Liquidator is a first-person shooter in Russian made and using the Build engine without an official license to it. There are three campaigns with a total of six maps.

465767.overview:
In 1992, Liverpool FC had been the UK's leading club for most of the previous 30 years, although their FA Cup success that year proved to be their last major trophy for nearly a decade. Arc Developments' licensed game features a third-person 3D view similar to Striker, with a small area of the screen in detail at a time, although there is also a scanner to view where players are on the full pitch.

Playing as Liverpool, you can play either the full season, single matches, a 2-player friendly, or the FA Cup in season. Each Liverpool player has a full profile (although they all look the same on the pitch, and are all depicted as white), and the formation and team lineup can be chosen.

469625.overview: Lynq bears striking similarities to another of Anarchy Entertainment's games, Too Many Geckos! The object here, like that more intriguingly-named game, is to match up the colored shapes on the different pieces so they all match. The pieces (pyramids) are displayed in three dimensions, so you'll need to rotate them around, and carefully change your viewpoint, to be able to match them properly. It certainly looks impressive, but overall it seems a bit overly-complicated for the core gameplay mechanic, especially with so many buttons that you need to press at the bottom of the screen.

470415.overview:
The Logic Master is a series of educational games for multiple systems.

The player challenges a number of educational logic games:

Analogies: Find the 2 similar words from a list.
Number Series: Complete a number series by filling in the last 2 numbers.
The Quest: Your quest is to locate the Dragon's Lair, which is hidden deep within the labyrinth. You must move through a series of tunnels, and fight or avoid the monsters that patrol the labyrinth. You can fight the labyrinth monsters by using your hero's ranged weapons. These weapons are found within chests that can be opened by correctly answering questions. Magical objects can be found in the labyrinth to help, including the magic amulet, health potion, and magic globe. The goal is to find the dragon, successfully answer its questions, and receive the treasure. There are 3 levels of difficulty.

470539.overview:
Last Duel: Inter Planet War 2012 follows the story of two planets that are at war with each other. On the planet Bacula, the Galden Tribe has overthrown the government and seized power over the whole world. Now they want more – by invading the peaceful planet of Mu and kidnapping Queen Sheeta.

The Mu-ans decided to take action. They asked their best scientists to come up with a weapon that will defeat the Galdens. After many long months, they were able to develop a vehicle of immense firepower, capable of leaping into the air to avoid ground hazards. In addition to that, it can transform into an airborne vessel whose purpose is to eliminate any kind of enemy in the sky.

Players have to guide their vehicle through six difficult levels - alternating between ground vehicle and fighter plane – while destroying every Galden that gets in their way. While progressing, holes in the ground need to be avoided, as players lose one of their ships should they happen to fall through one. Shooting power pods scattered around the level allows the player to increase their firepower. However, they lose that firepower if one of their ships is destroyed.

470542.overview: "Last Hero in China" is a side-scrolling beat'em-up game inspired by the 1993 movie of the same name, part of the "Once Upon a Time in China" film series. Players control Jet Li's character, Wong Fei-hung, a legendary martial arts master, as he progresses through levels defeating numerous opponents. The game features a total of 20 levels, with enemies ranging from ordinary fighters to "pumped" giants and bladed weapon users, and includes boss encounters such as a giant red centipede.

471070.overview: Little Willy is a platformer game that is inspired by Crystal Caves. The look and feel of the game, the layout of the main map (where you can choose from one of several levels to play) and even the main character looks quite similar. There is a brief story introduction (just start the game, it will automatically force you to watch it) and then you'll be jumping and shooting your way through many levels of one-hit deaths. The game controls well and provides infinite lives to try and try again!

471128.overview:
Locman I is an arcade game, which applies an idea used in Perestroika to an underwater adventure. The player is put in the flippers of the scuba diver on his hunt for the treasure of Atlantis after the deployment from a submarine. The goal of the game is to pass through all the underwater labyrinths, caves, wrecked ships and the ruins of ancient Atlantis, and to finally reach the magical island with a castle, where the new perils and adventures await.

On each fixed-screen level, the player directly controls the scuba diver, who should move between adjacent vertices of the path towards his goal. These vertices represent various objects, such as air bubbles, starfishes, fishes, shells, crabs, bottles, etc., which gradually grow smaller and eventually disappear, and new items appear to replace them. The player should always be on top of one of those items, if not one of the additional air tanks loses all its air. Certain underwater predators may either chase the scuba diver or wait in the hiding place to attack unexpectedly. Air tanks and precious pearls can be collected on the levels to increase the score. Transition between the levels is possible, when the transition vertex is found on the current level, it is one of vertices adjacent to the screen border. Levels can have several such vertices. Certain important items such as an underwater gun, key, or fuel for the boat should be found to advance in the game. Obtaining the gun, the scuba diver can shoot his enemies, but they will quickly re-spawn.

Highest scores are stored in the top twelve table.

472789.overview:
Pacman's clone comes from Spain, which has a number of features that are not impressive or interesting.

Firstly, the game was created by girls. Secondly, the levels are different from each other, and each place of respawn of ghosts eaten during the special bonus is located differently. Thirdly, there is a built-in level editor, if suddenly there is a person who wants to drive the famous "kolobok" through a labyrinth of his own creation. This is the end of the list of innovations.

It is difficult to say whether such a list will be enough for anyone to be interested in the game. The gameplay has remained the same, and no variety of maps in such conditions will help. Therefore, Luxman can be recommended only to fans of the original fun.

474726.overview:
Reon-ui Moheom ("Leon's Adventure") is a side-scrolling action platform game featuring an anthropomorphic lion as a protagonist. The plot revolves around a contest that will determine the new king of all animals. The protagonist sets out to compete, and will have to overcome various obstacles in his way.

The game plays in a fashion rather similar to Sonic the Hedgehog. Leon can jump, run and attack enemies at close range. Continuously pressing the run button speeds him up which is important because the levels are timed. Opposing the protagonist are various other anthropomorphic animals and even plants, each type with its own distinct behaviour and attack. Sometimes the enemies drop powerups when disposed of, including extra time added to the timer. Like Sonic, Leon collects golden rings, but here these can be used to purchase powerups between levels.

478034.overview:
"Lunar Landing is an early MS-DOS text-mode physics simulation game released in 1982. Representing the raw, hobbyist programming landscape of the IBM Personal Computer's debut era, this minimalist title strips away all visual graphics in favor of a pure mathematical and textual navigation interface. Players step into the role of a lunar module pilot trying to safely guide a spacecraft down onto the moon's surface using numerical console inputs.

The core gameplay operates as a turn-based calculation loop. Every round, the terminal displays the ship's current altitude, velocity, and remaining fuel reserves. The player must type in the exact number of pounds of fuel to burn for the next second of flight to counter the moon's gravity pull. Burning too little fuel causes the spacecraft to accelerate into a catastrophic high-velocity crash, while burning too much squanders precious fuel, leaving the module to drop helplessly once the tanks run dry. Reaching the surface at a perfectly safe terminal velocity requires precise mental math, capturing the authentic spirit of early mainframe-inspired computing."

478036.overview:
Lunar Commander 2 (1995) is a highly specialized hard-science space simulation game developed and published by VCSI Software for MS-DOS.

The Lineage Context: This game stands as the definitive and final enhanced iteration of a simulation engine lineage that originally began with Wesson International's Moonbase: A Lunar Colony Simulator (1990) and was later followed by Mallard Software's Lunar Command (1993).

The Design Reality: Rather than leaning into abstract science-fiction tropes or space combat, the game is famously built upon actual real-world NASA estimates and engineering logistics exploring the true feasibility of long-term outer space colonization.

The Gameplay Loop: Often described as a highly realistic, "spreadsheet-style" SimCity on the Moon, players are tasked with managing a lunar dome base infrastructure. You must manually route infrastructure grids, optimize power pipelines, and establish mining operations to harvest and sell resources like Helium and Oxygen back to Earth for expanding cash funds.

479578.overview: exter is an MS-DOS tile-based puzzle game released in 1993. Shifting away from action-oriented gameplay, the title tasks players with guiding the newly crowned King Lexter across 26 distinct, grid-aligned stages. Each environment presents a complex, maze-like arrangement of structural obstacles—including trees, fences, and geographical barriers—requiring careful route planning and spatial reasoning.The core gameplay operates on a strict, turn-based movement system constrained by a limited move counter for every stage. Players must decipher optimal pathways and avoid irreversible dead ends to guide King Lexter from his starting position to the designated exit portal. Exhibiting a clean top-down visual style characteristic of early-90s PC shareware, Lexter prioritizes intellectual optimization and tactical decision-making, standing as a textbook example of the era's minimalist, logic-driven PC puzzle design.

482535.overview: Léto s Oskarem (internationally known as Summer with Oscar) is a classic 2D cartoon point-and-click adventure game released for MS-DOS in 1998. Developed by a small team led by Pavel Širůček, it holds a significant place in Czech gaming history as the final adventure game published by Vochozka Trading right before the company transformed into the legendary studio Illusion Softworks (creators of the original Mafia and Hidden & Dangerous).

482736.overview: Tetris-style falling blocks share the playfield with small wandering lemmings. Completing a row introduces another lemming, and subsequent pieces can protect or crush it for points. Watch the moving characters while arranging blocks and clearing rows.
